boundaries.label: A feature slice — WALL: no cross-feature imports, no UI in Domain
Shared packages & platform — WALL: no feature code below

cards.title: The package graph is the enforcement
items: a target's `dependencies` list is the complete set of what it may import — a forbidden edge is a compile error, not a review comment
Domain targets are pure Swift: a SwiftUI import does not compile, and no URLSession, Keychain or FileManager reaches into Domain
the app target holds no business logic; the composition root builds AppEnvironment and hands each feature its adapters
feature UI never imports another feature's internals: shared capability is promoted into Kernel/UICore or duplicated through a port

cards.title: Ports: the consumer declares, the platform implements
items: InventoryRepository → SDK + GRDB adapter · SessionStore and TokenProvider → Keychain adapter · Navigator → router · Notifier → APNs/local adapter · Clock → system clock (tests use a fake)
ports speak domain types; no UIView or UIViewController crosses into Domain, and the ViewModel never holds a view
the Domain declares the port and the Data target implements it — the dependency arrow points at the port, never at the SDK

cards.title: UDF is the only presentation contract
items: one closed State enum, one Intent enum, effects on a single AsyncStream — a switch that misses a case does not compile
the ViewModel is @MainActor @Observable: `send(_ intent:)` is the entry point and the view only renders the state
the sealed state carries offline and forbidden, so every screen renders what can actually happen instead of three booleans

cards.title: Variants and the floor
items: three app targets share the feature and core packages; the market app never depends on the game engine or its entitlements
one variant = one app target = one binary; entitlements and usage strings are scoped per variant
a change that needs an exception re-cuts the layout — a config exception is a contract change, never a lint suppression
